title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Universal Store Person
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management (each director, the CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, Key Management Personnel and Board-designated persons), persons who work closely with Senior Management and/or in the finance or strategy team, IT staff with access to sensitive materials, any other employee who may come into possession of market sensitive information, and any other person the Board designates in writing. Also includes any company or trust controlled by such a person, and, for the purposes of section 4 (Blackout Periods/notification) only, a spouse, child, close relative, or person financially dependent on or acting in concert with such a person.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Board Chair; distinguished only for clearance purposes, where the Authorising Officer is the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Other directors, Company Secretary and any other Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, the Company Secretary, and any other Key Management Personnel; distinguished only for clearance purposes, where the Authorising Officer is the Chair of the Board or, in his/her absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Any other Universal Store Person
tiers.description: Universal Store Persons who are not the Chair, another director, Company Secretary or other KMP (e.g. staff who work closely with Senior Management, finance/strategy team members, IT staff with sensitive access); distinguished only for clearance purposes, where the Authorising Officer is the Chief Executive Officer.

definitions.hedging_definition: Operate to limit the economic risk of any Universal Store Person's security holding (e.g. hedging arrangements) including Universal Store's securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under any Universal Store incentive plan) on that Universal Store Person's behalf

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other period as a Blackout Period from time to time. Confidentiality of such additional periods is not addressed.

rules.detail: 'Protection arrangements' (defined to include instruments limiting economic risk, i.e. hedges, over Universal Store securities or 'Universal Store products in the derivatives markets') are banned outright, with no clearance route, over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of “protection arrangements” for any Universal Store securities (or Universal Store products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Universal Store securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Securities subject to a holding lock are expressly treated the same as unvested securities: protection arrangements are banned outright, with no clearance route.

rules.detail: Once vested and not subject to a holding lock, a protection arrangement (which would include an OTC put/call) requires the standard consent of the applicable Authorising Officer under paragraph 4.2.

Hedging arrangements are expressly named as an example of a protection arrangement; banned outright over unvested securities, including securities held beneficially under any Universal Store incentive plan.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested, unlocked securities requires the standard Authorising Officer consent under 4.2.
Monetisation is not named, but a structure that enables profit from a price decrease, or otherwise limits economic risk, is a protection arrangement; banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: Otherwise enable a Universal Store Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation structure over vested, unlocked securities is caught as a protection arrangement and requires standard 4.2 consent.
Short selling beyond a person's holding is expressly named as a protection arrangement, banned outright over unvested securities.

rules.detail: Short selling beyond a vested, unlocked holding requires standard 4.2 consent as a protection arrangement.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are expressly named as caught by the absolute ban on short-term or speculative dealing in the derivative markets. A non-speculative CFD that limits economic risk of a holding would separately be a protection arrangement under 5.2, banned for unvested/holding-locked securities and requiring consent otherwise.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Universal Store Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Universal Store securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Universal Store securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named anywhere. Only the consequence of a secured lender's enforcement disposal is addressed, as an exemption from the Policy's other restrictions (paragraph 6(a)(viii)).

Granting security, a charge or a pledge over Universal Store securities is not itself named, restricted or treated as a dealing; only the disposal that results from a secured lender's enforcement is addressed.

No provision restricts entering into a secured financing arrangement over Universal Store securities; only the resulting disposal upon a secured lender's enforcement of its rights is addressed, as an exemption.
Absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading, with no defined period (unlike the 3-month rules in comparable policies) and no stated clearance route.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Universal Store Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Universal Store securities.

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer for each Universal Store Person (the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Board Chair; the Chair of the Board, or in his/her absence the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, for other directors/the Company Secretary/other KMP; the CEO for any other Universal Store Person) has discretion, assessed case-by-case within the Board's absolute discretion as to what constitutes exceptional circumstances (including, without limitation, severe financial hardship or a court order), to approve dealing during a Blackout Period, or 'other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy' - wording broad enough to potentially reach the section 5.2(a) unvested/holding-lock protection-arrangement ban. Approval must be given in writing by email, and the standard notification requirements still apply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The entering into of all types of “protection arrangements” for any Universal Store securities (or Universal Store products in the derivatives markets): (a) is prohibited at any time in respect of any Universal Store securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock; and (b) otherwise, requires consent under paragraph 4.2.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar's put/call legs are squarely 'protection arrangements' (limiting economic risk and enabling profit from a price decrease); over unvested or holding-locked shares they are banned outright with no ordinary clearance route, but over vested, unrestricted shares they proceed with the standard 4.2 Authorising Officer consent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exceptional-circumstances override may reach the unvested ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances the Authorising Officer, has discretion to approve dealings in Universal Store securities during a Blackout Period, or other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This relief is unusually broad - not confined to Blackout Period trading - and its wording ('other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited') could arguably extend to the absolute unvested/holding-lock protection-arrangement ban, giving a possible, though untested, route to collar unvested shares with Authorising Officer approval on hardship or similar grounds.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lender enforcement exempted but must still be notified
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Universal Store securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement [is an exemption available at any time]. ... If a Universal Store Person undertakes any of the actions described in paragraph (a), that Universal Store Person must advise the relevant Authorising Officer
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is exempt from the Blackout Period and consent requirements, but the executive must still notify the Authorising Officer after the fact; there is no separate breach consequence stated for this scenario, unlike some peer policies.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no margin lending or general secured financing provision
bespoke_clauses.clause: (the Policy does not name margin lending and does not otherwise restrict entering a secured financing arrangement over Universal Store securities)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, if secured on vested shares, is not restricted by this Policy at all; only the resulting enforcement disposal is addressed, as an exemption.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Universal Store Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Universal Store securities. This prohibition includes short term direct dealing in Universal Store securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A short-tenor collar or one with early-termination features risks being characterised as short-term or speculative derivative-market trading, which is banned outright with no stated clearance route, so tenor and unwind mechanics should avoid that characterisation.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted (non-holding-locked) shares is achievable: the put and call are 'protection arrangements' under section 5.2 and, once vested and unlocked, require only the standard consent of the applicable Authorising Officer (the CEO for ordinary Universal Store Persons, the Board Chair or Audit and Risk Committee Chair for other directors/KMP, and the Audit and Risk Committee Chair for the Board Chair), plus the usual inside-information confirmation and Blackout Period avoidance. Over unvested or holding-locked shares the same protection arrangements are banned outright with no ordinary clearance route, though the unusually broad exceptional-circumstances override in 4.3 - which extends to 'other dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this policy', not just Blackout Period trading - may arguably reach even this ban, subject to the Board's absolute discretion on what counts as exceptional. There is no margin lending or secured-financing prohibition in the Policy, so the loan leg is unconstrained; if the bank later enforces its security and sells the shares, that disposal is expressly exempt from the Blackout Period and consent requirements (though the executive must still notify the Authorising Officer afterwards). The main residual risk is the undefined, no-exception ban on short-term or speculative trading, including in derivative-market instruments such as CFDs, so tenor and unwind mechanics should be structured to avoid that characterisation.
